common_name: Hawaiian Picture-Winged Giant Fly (Retinal & Wing Lacework Pigmentation)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila grimshawi (2.8 µm, detail scale)

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg (1979): du/dt = D_u lap u + gamma (a - u + u^2 v); dv/dt = D_v lap v + gamma (b - u^2 v)
equations.jacobian: f_u = gamma (-1 + 2 u0 v0); f_v = gamma u0^2; g_u = gamma (-2 u0 v0); g_v = -gamma u0^2
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = 0.5 * (tr + sqrt(tr^2 - 4 det)), tr = f_u + g_v - k^2 (D_u + D_v), det = (f_u - k^2 D_u)(g_v - k^2 D_v) - f_v g_u
equations.wavenumber: k_c = argmax_k sigma(k); lambda_c = 2 pi / k_c
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic Laplacian on the mode-growth patch; no-flux is not used

chronoseries_prediction.note: Same (a, b, gamma, D_u). Only delta = D_v/D_u changes. Wavelengths are argmax sigma(k), not the onset-formula k_c.

empirical_claims: Edwards et al. (2007) catalogued Hawaiian picture-wing diversity, including D. grimshawi, as a discrete set of wing-pigment patterns rather than a measured 2.8 µm Turing wavelength.
Werner et al. (2010) showed D. guttifera polka dots are Wingless-driven yellow melanin spots. That organ-scale mechanism is the successor's pattern, not a measurement of this detail-scale wavenumber.
Clark et al. (2007) sequenced the D. grimshawi genome as the Hawaiian picture-wing representative among the 12 Drosophila genomes.
The 2.765 µm wavelength is the slot's detail-scale calibration of the Schnakenberg fastest mode, not a length reported by those papers.
